title: Legion (Mark 5:1–13)
hookLine: a man among the tombs, chained and screaming, meets Jesus on the shore

lines: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE LAKE.
cards: The boat that came through the storm lands on the far shore: the other side in every sense: Gentile country, where people keep pigs. The first thing to meet Jesus is a man running at him from a graveyard.
He lives among the tombs. People have tried to chain him, hand and foot, and he snaps the chains. Night and day he cries out in the hills and hurts himself.
No man could tame him, Mark says. By any measure the town has, he's too far gone.

teach.b: Mark tells every detail of the horror, then the strangest turn. The man runs to Jesus and falls on his knees. The voice that comes out of him shouts: what have I to do with thee, Jesus, Son of the most high God?
Jesus asks a simple, human question: what's your name?

In the King James Bible the answer is chilling: "My name is Legion: for we are many." A legion was a unit of the Roman army, a Latin word carried into Mark's Greek. So the man has no name of his own anymore.
Just a crowd, an army, inside him. Some readers hear an edge there too: in a land under Roman rule, a man possessed by a legion.
The spirits beg to be sent into a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside, and Jesus lets them.

teach.h: A HERD RUSHES INTO THE LAKE.
teach.b: The herd, about two thousand, Mark says, rushes down the steep bank into the lake. It's a wild, unsettling scene, and Mark doesn't explain all of it.
What he's clear on is the man: living among the dead, beside animals the law of Moses calls unclean, out of reach of chains and neighbors. And Jesus crossed a storm to get to him.
Churches differ on how to speak about what troubled him: some read the story alongside illness of the mind, and others stress that it describes spiritual forces too.
What the story itself shows is plain: a man nobody could reach, reached.

how: Many Christians pray by name for people who are suffering in mind or spirit, and churches offer pastoral care, and in some traditions prayers of deliverance, alongside medical and mental health care.

games.q: you've just crossed a storm. on the shore, a man everyone fears comes running from the tombs, shouting. what does Jesus do?
o: wait for the locals to restrain him.
games.why: he asks, what is thy name? my name is Legion: for we are many. then he sets him free.

practice: Let one person come to mind who is struggling badly right now, with addiction, despair, illness of the mind, a life that feels lived among the tombs, maybe someone everyone else has given up on, and hold their real name, the one underneath the struggle.
If you pray, pray for them by that name; if you don't, hold them in mind with as much care as you can. If that person is you, you're allowed to hold yourself the same way, and to reach out for help.

wordCard.voice: Legion. A Roman army unit, and the name a tormented man gives when he's lost his own: we are many.

orig.note: Greek, from the Latin legio: a unit of the Roman army.

carryVoice: Your line: no one is too far. Jesus crossed a storm to reach him. Day one hundred seventy-six, complete.
